scenes.heading: Simplifying surds
scenes.sub: Exact answers, written as neatly as possible
scenes.say: Exact answers in Year 10 are often surds, like root fifty or six root two. Let’s get fast at writing any surd in its simplest form.
scenes.caption: Exact answers in Year 10 are often surds, like √50 or 6√2. Let’s get fast at writing any surd in its simplest form.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Square bundles can be unpacked and carried out of the suitcase
scenes.science: Perfect-square factors leave the root as their square root
scenes.breaks: Real bundles don’t shrink when you carry them. It is a picture of √(k²) = k.
scenes.say: Think of the number under the root as a suitcase. Anything packed in a perfect square bundle, like four, nine or thirty-six, can be carried outside, but it shrinks to its square root on the way out. Thirty-six comes out as six. Anything else stays inside.

scenes.heading: Where is √50?
scenes.say: First a number line from five to nine. Seven squared is forty-nine and eight squared is sixty-four, so root fifty sits just past seven. A surd is irrational, but it still has an exact place on the line.
scenes.caption: A number line from 5 to 9. 7² = 49 and 8² = 64, so √50 sits just past 7. A surd is irrational, but it still has an exact place on the line.

scenes.heading: Simplify √n
scenes.say: The method. Find the largest perfect square factor. For one hundred and eighty it is thirty-six. Split the root into root thirty-six times root five. Root thirty-six is six, so the answer is six root five.
scenes.caption: Find the largest perfect square factor. For 180 it is 36. Split: √180 = √36 × √5. √36 = 6, so the answer is 6√5.

scenes.heading: Which is larger?
scenes.question: Which is larger: 3√7 or 2√15?
scenes.say: Which is larger, three root seven or two root fifteen? Make each an entire surd. Three root seven is root sixty-three. Two root fifteen is root sixty. Sixty-three is bigger, so three root seven is larger.
scenes.caption: Which is larger, 3√7 or 2√15? Make each an entire surd: 3√7 = √63 and 2√15 = √60. 63 is bigger, so 3√7 is larger.

scenes.heading: Exact lengths with Pythagoras
scenes.say: Here is a right-angled triangle with shorter sides eight and four centimetres. x squared is sixty-four plus sixteen, which is eighty. Sixteen is the biggest square factor of eighty, so x is four root five centimetres.
scenes.caption: A right-angled triangle with sides 8 cm and 4 cm. x² = 64 + 16 = 80. 16 is the biggest square factor of 80, so x = 4√5 cm.

points: Take out the largest square factor
Prime factors: each pair comes out as one
scenes.say: Recap. Take out the largest perfect square factor. With prime factors, each pair comes out as one. To make an entire surd, square the coefficient and multiply it in, and compare surds that way. Check by squaring your answer. Now try the practice questions!
